newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev falls to 266-267.50 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev falls to 266-267.50 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev fell to 266.00-267.50 per dollar in nervous morning trade on the interbank market from 260.00/50 at Wednesday's close as dollar supply trailed far behind demand, dealers said.
"Final clients have been actively bidding for dollars since the opening but supply is extremely low," a commercial bank dealer said.
"The central bank seems to be the only one actively offering foreign currency this morning and if demand remains as high as it is the lev may fall beyond 270," another dealer said.
The central bank began to sell dollars at 262.50 levs at the opening and raised its dollar asks to 265-266 levs by 1030 local time (0830 GMT), dealers said.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
Foreign currency demand also rose on the cash market which put an additional pressure on the lev, traders said.
The longer value date of today's spot deals was also a reason for the lev fall, dealers said.
"But the slide (from Wednesday's close) due to the longer value date should have been three levs per dollar at most," another dealer said.
Banks and foreign exchange bureaux sold cash dollars to clients between 268-270 levs, traders said. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-876032
